messages:
acme-mobile: Hey, streaming is failing for one of our Android users. They start a chat generation and midway through the SSE the client drops and they get a 0-length event. Happens when they switch from office Wi‑Fi to their phone hotspot. Repro steps attached.

evan_support: Thanks — can you paste the client logs and the request id? Also does this happen consistently when switching networks or only sometimes?

acme-mobile: Happens ~6/10 times during the transfer. Here are the logs from the client (Android, okhttp SSE lib):

```
I/StreamClient: SSE open id=conn-88 req=rid_4f2a
I/StreamClient: chunk: data: {"delta":"hello"}\n\n
W/Network: network lost (TYPE_WIFI)
I/StreamClient: attempting reconnect
E/StreamClient: read timed out after 17s
I/StreamClient: reconnect with Last-Event-ID: 0f2a
I/StreamClient: got partial event: data: {"delta":" wor"
I/StreamClient: connection closed by server code=1006
```

acme-mobile: Request id on Redwood side: r-7c9b1f. Happens using our app's in-app network switch; Chrome mobile SSE seems more resilient.

jamila_sre: Got it. I pulled the server-side logs for r-7c9b1f: saw a 502 from our edge right around the network switch, then the connection removed from the instance LRU (evicted CVK). Snippet:

```
[2026-03-12T15:22:41.123Z] INFO conn=conn-88 req=r-7c9b1f stream=open
[2026-03-12T15:22:58.534Z] WARN upstream=gw-42 peer-reset (connection reset by peer)
[2026-03-12T15:22:58.536Z] INFO conn=conn-88 server-close code=1006 reason="upstream reset"
```

jamila_sre: That upstream reset corresponds to the client's network change. Looks like our edge closed the socket when the client's TCP 4‑way handshake didn't complete in time.

eli_eng: Two quick things to check on the client: 1) are you setting a reasonably short TCP keepalive/heartbeat on the SSE client? 2) are you supporting Last-Event-ID on reconnect so the server can resume from the last sent chunk? Many mobile libs don't reattach event ids automatically.

acme-mobile: We do set Last-Event-ID in our reconnect path. Heartbeat is default on okhttp which is ~20s. We do see the partial event where the JSON is truncated.

evan_support: From Redwood side we have two levers: increase idle timeout on the edge for that tenant (tunable) and enable early event flushing (we can push partial chunks sooner so client can ACK). But the correct pattern is to make reconnect resume idempotently.

acme-mobile: Any recommended server-side config? This is for a dedicated customer instance.

jamila_sre: For Dedicated we can bump the keepalive window for the tenant's edge from 15s to 45s and enable aggressive TCP retransmit for short-lived handoffs. I'll open an infra change PR but need approval.

eli_eng: Also share this with your Android engineer — we've seen the okhttp client drop connections on network change unless you call EventSource#close and then re-open with the same Last-Event-ID. If you just let the socket hang, the OS may yank the TCP and you lose the final buffer.

acme-mobile: We're doing close+reopen but might be recreating the SSE object without setting Last-Event-ID. We'll add a repro build tomorrow.

oncall-bot: Incident 2026-03-12-88 created: customer acme-mobile streaming-drop hotspot switch. Pagerduty notified (pgd-331). Ops change requested.

evan_support: In the meantime I can apply a tenant-level edge timeout increase for a few hours to mitigate while you ship a client fix. Want me to do that?

acme-mobile: Yes please — that'd be great. Also can you surface any headers we should log to correlate drops? Our client can capture the Server-Sent-Event id header and Redwood request id.

jamila_sre: Add X-Redwood-ReqId and Last-Event-ID to logs. I'll add a short note in the deployment PR to log upstream resets and peer-close reasons.

eli_eng: And to prevent truncated JSON events, consider sending explicit chunk terminators on the server: send a zero-length comment line `:heartbeat` every 6s so client-side parsers don't buffer partial data for too long.

acme-mobile: Good tip. We'll try heartbeat + ensure Last-Event-ID is preserved on reconnect. Any recommended retry backoff pattern?

evan_support: Exponential backoff starting at 500ms up to 5s for reconnects looks fine. Also preserve the streaming payload buffer; only drop if you get a new stream that replays from an earlier event id.

acme-mobile: Thanks. We'll roll a client patch tomorrow and report back. For the edge bump — thanks in advance.

deploy-bot: deploy user=jamila target=tenant-edge/t-198 config=keepalive=45s — queued

jamila_sre: Deploy queued, will watch. I'll also add a short kb note in #support and link the p90 trace for r-7c9b1f.

acme-mobile: Appreciate the help. I'll paste client repro instructions and an APK once the build is ready. :pray:

evan_support: Closing loop — if you still see partial events after client fix + edge bump, we'll capture a tcpdump during the handoff and escalate to networking.

acme-mobile: Will do. Thanks all.
